## Why This Is Asked
Tests validate ML model changes without degrading production performance, especially drift and rollback safety.

## Key Concepts
- Data drift detection
- Canary deployment
- Feature store integration
- Observability and SLOs
- Safe rollback policies

## Code Example
```python
import math

def kl_div(p, q):
    return sum(pi * math.log(pi/qi) for pi, qi in zip(p, q) if pi > 0 and qi > 0)

def drift_exceeds(p, q, thr=0.1):
    return kl_div(p, q) > thr
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you automate rollback when drift or latency thresholds are breached?
- What tests ensure user data privacy during shadow/live testing?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

In fintech-like domains, event-sourced architectures are common and replay safety critical. This question probes experience with end-to-end validation, idempotency, and exactly-once guarantees under stress.

## Key Concepts

- Event sourcing and CQRS
- Idempotent event handlers and deduplication
- Exactly-once processing and out-of-order delivery
- Replay scenarios, rollback, and read-model consistency

## Code Example

```javascript
function applyEvent(state, event) {
  const id = event.aggregateId + ':' + event.sequence
  if (state.seen && state.seen[id]) return state // idempotent guard
  // apply logic depending on event.type
  const next = { ...state, data: {/* updated */}, seen: { ...(state.seen || {}), [id]: true } }
  return next
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you simulate out-of-order delivery and replay in CI?
- What metrics and dashboards would you use to detect drift between write models and read models?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Real-time collaboration is core to many products; CRDTs guarantee convergence but testing must cover offline-to-online sync, partitions, and durability.

## Key Concepts
- CRDT invariants (confluence, commutativity, idempotence)
- Offline-first and multi-device sync
- Partition tolerance and recovery
- Performance budgets and data integrity

## Code Example
```javascript
// Simple CRDT merge sketch
function merge(a, b) {
  // pseudo-merge: union of ops; assumes op histories
  return { ...a, ops: [...new Set([...(a.ops||[]), ...(b.ops||[])])] }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you simulate network partitions in CI?
- How would you extend tests for document rewrite conflicts or undo/redo?
